actualChain.fact: decision-choose receives a new real human admission, enters business.withCase and invokes mutations.recordChoice. The final check at line64 maps a failed host.revalidate to decision-authority-changed regardless of the inner result.

withCase reads the current case before installing a request-bound private case selection. It does not hold an all-domain persistence transaction around the action. After the action it revalidates the same Request, binding, selected case and scope, then releases the scope.

recordChoice checks real human intent/replay, loads C08, compares the real two stored scenarios with the registered criterion, verifies the selected alternative and baseline, obtains domain choice values, then saves the actual ChoiceRecord. It does not accept a caller-supplied comparison output or a fabricated metric.

The installed criterion registry only accepts planner:known-subtotal-difference with a real sensitivity binding, its issued unit, source evidence, current case and stored baseline. Omitting sensitivity would fail the installed contract.

Each completed metric read issues real sensitivity units, computes the real preview, then resolves the rule and issues the units again before returning. No earlier HTTP units result is accepted as authority for this new action.

resolveChoiceValues reopens the case, resolves the rule and reads the metric twice, then reopens the case and human authority. Thus this stage alone would require at least four units.issue calls for the one criterion if it completed. This is static fanout, not proof that the failed run reached this stage or a measured duration.

The private UI admission uses a fixed five-minute expiry. current(), requestFor() and revalidate() require the live real admission. Renewal of the public Procurement period before a route does not renew that route's separate UI lease.

applicability.evidence: Lines54–56 require a nonempty preparedChanges collection, all planned Procurement changes and no receipts. Our real case is before its first ChoiceRecord and before C12 prepare; it has no prepared changes. It returns to the canonical reader outside the scope. The published owner test20c02e25, lines129–138, explicitly preserves this fallback for a chosen case without a prepared change (canonical1, inside0, contexts2, resolutions4). That test source was inspected, not run here.

The sf-procurement record is in the wrapper's possible entry scope, so this is not labeled entirely off-path. business c851 lines135–143 passes only decisionEvidence.resolveEvidence as its canonical resolver. decision-host23d9 lines255–260/284–288 reads a protected archive; missing archive returns undefined. That archive is produced by captureSource in prepareDomainCommands, which this fixture has not called. BCS5cca lines263–265 then calls currentProcurement after the wrapper promise resolves. The wrapper permits undefined as canonical fresh-source fallthrough (lines98–107). It therefore does not enclose the current PR revalidation or the entire mixed case/criterion chain. Its extra scope checks have no measured benefit here.

Completed observations are scoped to actual recall/observe invocations with exact Request/binding/selection/reader/snapshot fences. decision-choose is not a recall invocation. Its eligibility also excludes the mixed Planner and PR alternative bases used here. Ordinary reads delegate to procurementCaseRead, which falls back as above.

The new invocation-local completed-proof branch is restricted to duplicated scenarios backed by exact Procurement record refs and createSfScenarioProcurementProofScope2ebb. Our candidate operation addresses the genuine Planner service component and Planner base; the baseline has no operation. It retains the canonical Planner branch. It cannot be made eligible by substituting a PR reference for the Planner target.

This reader borrows currentSnapshots only inside a real active provider transaction, retaining full snapshot, source, Request and authority fences after awaits. Outside a provider scope it retains transactionAll. withCase does not establish such a transaction around choice, and the candidate case scope is ineligible. No runtime evidence establishes that this helper would shorten the failed choice.

ownCorrectionAssessment.usefulExistingCorrections: The same-value real Planner parameter, strict one-hypothetical-component assertions and a fresh public Procurement selection before each action are exercised successfully up to units and criterion registration. Do not remove them.
rejected: Removing sensitivity or using empty criteria changes or violates the real criterion/choice contract.

Reusing a units or comparison receipt as current authority, constructing a ChoiceRecord, replacing Planner targetRef by a PR ref, or inserting an archive/prepared change would fabricate the missing prerequisite.
Renewing inside an in-flight action, extending TTL/deadline or caching authority suppresses the actual refusal.
Selecting a smaller period or fewer cost categories changes the current annual mission's tested coverage inventory and is not a correction for this refusal.
Switching to a direct private mutation path would bypass the installed route under examination and would not validate the public choice consumer.
ownCorrectionAssessment.boundedFixtureObservation: initializeWp12ScenarioSources materializes three raw Forecast versions; each Purchase case selects only baseline plus its one variant and promotes exactly two. The third raw version is unselected in that variant, so a future separate fixture-only reduction could omit it while preserving selected data, annual period and assertions. This does not remove a selected case read or the mandatory metric fanout, and there is no evidence that it resolves the approximately300-second choice. It is not recommended as justification for another equivalent run.
